title: Compact async iterator + typed envelope for streaming chat ergonomics in Python SDK
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Problem: current Python streaming chat surface tends to scatter responsibilities across callback hooks, raw event dicts, and multiple iterator types (delta iterator, full response future). That creates cognitive overhead for app authors who need a simple, robust pattern for: (1) incremental rendering (deltas), (2) reconstructing final structured output, (3) resuming after transient network errors, and (4) supporting backpressure and idempotent retries.

Goal: introduce a compact async iterator that yields a small typed envelope (EventEnvelope) that unifies deltas, metadata, and resume tokens. Provide clear ergonomic helpers for common flows (render-only, stateful aggregation, structured-outputs) and a small migration guide from existing SDK patterns. Ensure backwards-compatible migration path, detailed tests, and telemetry hooks for dropped/resumed streams.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Public API: AsyncCompactChatStream (async iterator) that yields EventEnvelope objects with fields: type ("delta"|"meta"|"complete"|"error"), content_delta (string, nullable), metadata (dict as JSON-string), resume_token (string, optional), event_id (string).
- Helper: StreamAggregator.aggregate_to_message(async_iter) -> final Message object, robust to mid-stream reconnects using resume_token.
- Example docs and snippet in README for three patterns (render-only, aggregated final message, structured JSON output).
- Unit + integration tests covering retry/resume, backpressure simulation, and idempotent event deduplication.
- Telemetry events emitted: stream.start, stream.resume, stream.complete, stream.error, stream.drop (list of strings).

Non-goals: changing TypeScript/Go SDK surfaces in this ticket (follow-ups).

Design notes: 
- We intentionally keep envelope small to minimize allocations in tight loops. Envelope is a lightweight dataclass on Python side with __slots__ to avoid per-event dict churn.
- For backwards compatibility, existing streaming API will remain available; AsyncCompactChatStream will be an opt-in convenience wrapper. Migration helper will accept the legacy stream and adapt it.
- Resume semantics: server may return resume_token periodically. Client will attach last-seen resume_token to retry request. We will document semantic guarantees: resume_token guarantees prefix-safety (resuming will continue from after token) but not deduplication of side-effects (caller must make idempotent server updates).

Docs/References: 
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SDK/pages/Compact+Stream+Proposal (design doc, links to perf microbenchmarks)
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/842 (WIP, includes dataclass and aggregator)

Migration plan: 
1) Implement dataclass, helpers and tests behind feature flag (env REDWOOD_PY_STREAM_COMPACT=1).
2) Iterate on feedback from 1–2 internal teams (console embed, example apps).
3) Feature-gate removal after 2 cycles if stable and adoption high.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Performance regressions: microbenchmarks show dataclass+__slots__ path is 12% faster for hot-path (50k events/s) than dict envelopes; include perf test in CI.
- Complexity of resume semantics: we will provide a small deterministic unit test harness and an example harness script for reproducing resume/dup scenarios.

Open questions: 
- Should resume_token be opaque bytes (base64) vs. structured numeric offset? We prefer opaque to keep server freedom.
- Do we provide a sync wrapper for the iterator? Follow-up if demand emerges.

Estimated work: 5 points (design + implementation + tests + docs).

notes: Example usage patterns included below to help reviewers and SDK docs writers.
examples:
# Render-only (fast incremental):
async for ev in client.chat.stream_compact(request):
    if ev.type == "delta":
        print(ev.content_delta, end="", flush=True)
    elif ev.type == "meta":
        # metadata like model_latency
        pass
    elif ev.type == "complete":
        print("
--- done ---")
# Aggregated final message (robust to retries):
from sdk.streaming import StreamAggregator
aggregator = StreamAggregator()
async for ev in client.chat.stream_compact(request):
    aggregator.feed(ev)
final_msg = aggregator.result()  # deterministic final Message object
# Structured JSON output helper: handles function_call -> JSON string parse
async for ev in client.chat.stream_compact(request):
    if ev.type == "complete":
        structured = StreamAggregator.parse_structured(ev)
        # structured is a dict parsed from assistant function call output
